2608.03890.title: CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement
2608.03890.paper_summary: A clinically useful chest X-ray system must go beyond fluent report generation: it should classify findings with tunable decision thresholds, localize them spatially, and derive the anatomical measurements upon which many diagnoses depend. Today's Vision-Language Models (VLMs) treat these as separate problems, if they address them at all, leaving a gap between what radiologists need and what generative models provide. We introduce CARE-X, a chest X-ray VLM that narrows this gap by unifying auxiliary discriminative supervision with reward-aligned generation. CARE-X augments its generative backbone with focal-loss classification and composite-loss grounding heads, co-trained alongside the language-modeling objective. This auxiliary supervision produces discriminative diagnostic predictions with tunable decision thresholds and precise spatial localization while also improving report quality, providing evidence that structured prediction and generation reinforce one another. Building on this foundation, Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization (DAPO) leverages task-specific reward signals for report generation, visual question answering (VQA), and spatial grounding, directly optimizing the clinical quality metrics that matter in practice. The result is state-of-the-art performance on the majority of metrics across four report-generation benchmarks, 94.0% VQA accuracy on ReXVQA (+6.0 pp over the next-best baseline), and generative spatial decoding that reaches near parity with dedicated detection heads. Separately, to address measurement-dependent diagnoses, we couple Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with native tool-calling capabilities for invoking deterministic measurement tools, while retaining full visual access to the image. This hybrid inference yields +43.6 pp average F1 over perception-only baselines across five measurement-dependent conditions.
2608.03890.paper_summary_zh: 一個臨床上有用的胸部X光系統必須超越流暢的報告生成：它應該具備可調的決策閾值來分類發現，並能夠進行空間定位，還要推導出許多診斷所依賴的解剖測量。當今的視覺-語言模型（VLMs）將這些視為獨立的問題，如果有處理的話，則在放射科醫生的需求和生成模型提供的之間留下了空白。我們介紹了CARE-X，一個胸部X光VLM，通過將輔助的判別監督與獎勵對齊的生成統一起來，縮小了這一空白。CARE-X通過焦點損失分類和複合損失定位頭增強其生成主幹，並與語言建模目標共同訓練。這種輔助監督產生了具有可調決策閾值和精確空間定位的判別診斷預測，同時改善了報告質量，提供了結構化預測和生成相互強化的證據。在此基礎上，解耦Clip和動態採樣策略優化（DAPO）利用任務特定的獎勵信號進行報告生成、視覺問題回答（VQA）和空間定位，直接優化在實踐中重要的臨床質量指標。結果是在四個報告生成基準中大多數指標上達到最先進的性能，在ReXVQA上達到94.0%的VQA準確率（比下一個最佳基準高出6.0個百分點），以及生成的空間解碼接近專用檢測頭的水平。此外，為了解決依賴測量的診斷，我們將Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct與本地工具調用功能結合，以調用確定性的測量工具，同時保留對圖像的完整視覺訪問。這種混合推理在五種依賴測量的條件下，平均F1比僅感知的基準高出43.6個百分點。
